brief.subject: Werner warns on Q3 costs; truckload capacity still not rebounding
brief.headline: Werner Flags Rising Costs as Truckload Capacity Shows No Recovery
brief.dek: Werner blames fuel, driver and claims costs for a Q3 miss, capacity stays stuck, and a nuclear verdict against C.H. Robinson stands.
brief.lede: Werner Enterprises warned Monday that Q3 profit will fall short, pointing to the same fuel, driver and insurance claims costs squeezing small carriers.

sections.heading: Werner Issues Q3 Profit Warning
bullets: Werner preannounced weaker third-quarter earnings Monday, a sign that even large fleets are struggling with costs.
Fuel, driver pay and insurance claims were cited as the drivers, which are the same pressures hitting owner-operators.
Box truck operator Telly Arnold says newcomers often learn about insurance deposits, claims and breakdowns only after chasing revenue.
Know your cost per mile before booking loads; thin margins leave little room for surprise expenses.

sections.heading: Truckload Capacity Still Not Recovering
bullets: Despite months of rate inflation, data shows no sign that truckload capacity is coming back.
Many in the market expected a rebound by now, so carriers should plan around current conditions rather than a quick turnaround.

sections.heading: Legal Risk Stays High
bullets: A Texas judge affirmed the nuclear verdict against C.H. Robinson, keeping large-verdict risk front and center for insurers.
Big verdicts that hold up on appeal tend to feed into the claims costs carriers see at renewal.
A California trucking company owner pleaded guilty in a $2.1M identity theft scheme affecting nearly 100 people.

sections.heading: Peak Season Signals
bullets: DHL Group raised its 2026 outlook on expectations for a strong peak season.
FedEx and UPS delivery prices are set for a record-high Q4 as peak surcharges kick in, according to the TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index.
Port of Savannah plans a 3.5M TEU terminal and expects to handle 12 million TEUs annually once it is built.

sections.heading: Border Freight Under Pressure
bullets: A U.S. trucking crackdown is raising concerns about freight disruptions on Mexico cross-border lanes.
Carriers running border freight should watch for delays and shifting demand as enforcement tightens.
